# Add-ons

Godot add-ons of autoload-dev, built with the rules of this repository and consumed by Godot
applications through Bazel. Every add-on brings its native SDKs.

Each directory here is a Bazel module of its own, with its own `MODULE.bazel`, version and
release tags:

<!-- Generated by `mise run addons:generate`: the add-on modules. -->

| Module | Add-ons | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`autoload_sentry`](sentry) | [Sentry for Godot](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-godot) for Godot applications built with Bazel: crash and error reporting on Android, iOS, Linux and macOS. | 0.1.0 |

<!-- End of the generated add-on modules. -->

There is one module per add-on, or per group of add-ons that must be versioned together
because they share one SDK. Each module keeps its example applications in its `examples/`
directory: a root module that consumes the add-ons like an external application.

## Use in an application

Depend on the module's release, as its README shows:

```starlark
bazel_dep(name = "autoload_<module>", version = "0.1.0")
```

Before a module is on the Bazel Central Registry, the release notes of its tag show the
`archive_override` that fetches the release's archive. To use a commit instead, take the
module's directory as `strip_prefix`:

```starlark
archive_override(
    module_name = "autoload_<module>",
    integrity = "sha256-...",
    strip_prefix = "rules_godot-<commit>/addons/<module>",
    urls = ["https://github.com/autoload-dev/rules_godot/archive/<commit>.tar.gz"],
)
```

The add-ons need a rules_godot that matches them: use an override for `autoload_rules_godot`
at the same commit until a release has what they need.

## A new add-on

`mise run addon:new <module>` creates a module with one add-on, `mise run addon:new <module>
--addon <addon>` adds an add-on to a module. Both write from the template in
[tools/addons/template](../tools/addons/template), which builds on Android, iOS, the editor
and desktop from the start. The [add-on guidance](AGENTS.md) describes the layout.

## Releases

Every module is released on its own, with tags named `<module>-v<version>`, such as
`autoload_<module>-v0.1.0`. The tag's commit has the same `version` in the module's
`MODULE.bazel`, and its release notes show the `bazel_dep` to add.
